scope_notes: Covers fastpitch hitting (stance/load, stride, swing, finish), windmill pitching, infield fielding and overhand throwing. Slapping, bunting, catching and outfield play are not yet covered.
source_gap_notes: Strong peer-reviewed coverage exists for windmill pitching loads; hitting/fielding mechanics rely mainly on elite college/Olympic coaches and NFCA/USA Softball materials (several are paid videos whose public descriptions were used). Fewer than 10 tier-1 sources; tier-2/3 coaching sources fill the gap and are labelled.

sources.name: USA Softball (ASA) instructional video catalog - Mike Candrea 'Fundamentals of Hitting', Ralph Weekly hitting/circuit videos
sources.author_or_org: USA Softball / M. Candrea, R. Weekly
sources.credibility: Official USA Softball instructional series by Olympic head coaches Candrea and Weekly; covers stance, load, strike and swing plus 25+ USA Olympic team drills.

sources.name: USA Softball 2026 High Performance Program Operations Manual (player evaluations)
sources.credibility: National governing body's evaluation protocol: what national-team evaluators grade (hitting mechanics/power/timing, exit velocity, pitch speed/location/movement).

sources.name: NFCA - Softball Hitting Drills: 4 Top Drills (Chidester sequencing, Road Map drill, Strub two-plate drill)
sources.credibility: National Fastpitch Coaches Association, drills from NCAA head coaches.

sources.name: NFCA Practice Plans and Drills - Year One Package
sources.credibility: NFCA's structured practice plans and numbered drills for fielding and throwing.

sources.name: Ehren Earleywine - Hitting Mechanics and Drills for Softball (Softball Hitting Absolutes + 24 drills)
sources.credibility: Three-time Women's College World Series coach (Missouri); breaks the swing into 10 phases with video analysis of elite vs beginner hitters.

sources.name: Ehren Earleywine - Infield Mechanics and Drills for Softball
sources.credibility: NFCA Coach of the Year; covers routine grounders, glove work, footwork and why a 3/4 arm slot is preferred for infield throws.

sources.name: Megan Smith - Fundamentals and Techniques for Record Breaking Middle & Corner Infield Play
sources.credibility: Division I head coach; 27 infield drills incl. drop-step and 'Hot Dog' drills.

sources.name: University of Georgia open textbook - Softball: Fundamentals, Skills & Strategies
sources.credibility: University course text with explicit fielding/throwing technique and progressions.

sources.name: Kinematics and Kinetics of Elite Windmill Softball Pitching (AJSM)
sources.credibility: 3D analysis of 24 elite pitchers at the 1996 Olympics; shoulder distraction ~80% body weight; 7 mechanics variables explain 69% of shoulder distraction.

sources.name: Biomechanics of Youth Windmill Softball Pitching (AJSM)
sources.credibility: 53 youth pitchers; shoulder distraction ~94% BW; stride-foot vertical and braking forces exceed body weight.

sources.name: Biomechanics of Windmill Softball Pitching With Implications About Injury Mechanisms at the Shoulder and Elbow (JOSPT)
sources.author_or_org: Barrentine SW, Fleisig GS et al.
sources.credibility: ASMI group (Barrentine, Fleisig, Escamilla, Andrews); compressive forces 70-98% BW at elbow/shoulder; biceps-labrum complex at risk.

sources.name: Biceps Activity During Windmill Softball Pitching (AJSM)
sources.credibility: EMG: biceps activity higher in windmill than overhand throwing, peaking (eccentric) at the 9 o'clock and follow-through phases.

sources.name: Variables associated with peak throwing-shoulder distraction force in high school softball pitchers (AJSM)
sources.credibility: Greater trunk flexion at foot contact and faster elbow flexion were associated with LOWER shoulder distraction force.

sources.name: Windmill Pitching: Drive Phase with Chanda Bell (Marshall University) - Coaches Insider
sources.credibility: NCAA D-I pitching coach instructional on the drive/push-off phase.

sources.name: The Hitting Vault - Softball Hitting Drills and Practice Plans
sources.credibility: Hitting-instruction organization; tee/front-toss/live progressions and contact-position cues. Tier 3.

sources.name: StriveOn - Softball Pitching Drills: 15 Windmill Drills for Every Level
sources.credibility: Coaching-platform drill compilation incl. the K / power-position drill. Tier 3.

sources.name: Softball Spot - Windmill Pitching Drills for Beginners
sources.credibility: Widely used beginner progression (wrist snaps -> half circles -> full circles). Tier 3.

skills.name: Batting: stance and load
skills.recommended_camera: Side view from the open side (facing the hitter's chest) at hip height, plus a rear view from behind the catcher for head/stride direction; 120+ fps if available.

checkpoints.description: Athletic, balanced stance: feet roughly shoulder-width or slightly wider, knees flexed, weight on the balls/inside of the feet.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: ankle-to-ankle distance about 1.0-1.5x shoulder width; knee flexion visible (knee angle ~150-165 deg)

checkpoints.description: Hands set near the rear shoulder with the bat knob roughly pointing down/toward the catcher's feet; relaxed grip.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: wrists within ~1 forearm length of the rear shoulder; wrists above elbow height

checkpoints.description: Load ('negative move'): weight shifts slightly onto the rear leg and the front hip/shoulder turn inward while the hands drift back - the head stays nearly still.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: pelvis rotates slightly closed (toward catcher) during load; horizontal head displacement small (< ~1 head-width) from stance to end of load

checkpoints.description: Eyes level and both eyes on the pitcher (head turned, not tilted).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: line between eyes within ~10-15 deg of horizontal

faults.name: Over-loading / swaying back
faults.video_signs: Head and hips drift toward the catcher during the load; rear knee collapses outside the rear foot.
faults.correction_cue: 'Load into your back hip, not past it - keep your head over your belt buckle.'
faults.why_it_matters: Head movement changes eye level and timing; excess drift must be recovered before rotating.

faults.name: Bat wrap / barrel tipping
faults.video_signs: Bat barrel wraps behind the head pointing at the pitcher, lengthening the swing path.
faults.correction_cue: 'Keep the knob pointing down and the barrel above your hands.'
faults.why_it_matters: A wrapped barrel creates a long, casting path to the ball.

faults.name: Rigid, upright stance
faults.video_signs: Knees locked, weight on heels, minimal flexion.
faults.correction_cue: 'Athletic position - like a shortstop ready for a ground ball.'
faults.why_it_matters: Locked joints slow the start of the swing and kill rhythm.

drills.name: Back-wall load drill
drills.setup: Hitter sets up with the rear hip about a fist away from a wall or net behind them, bat in hand.
steps: Take a normal stance.
Load into the rear hip while keeping the head still.
The rear hip/glute may lightly touch the wall; the head and rear knee must NOT drift past the rear foot.
Hold the loaded position for 2 seconds, then reset.
drills.dosage: 3 sets x 8 slow reps, then 5 reps at game speed
drills.why: Gives instant tactile feedback on how far the hips may move, teaching a rotational load rather than a lateral sway so the eyes stay level.

pro_tips.tip: Earleywine separates hitting 'absolutes' (must be present in every good swing) from personal 'styles' (stance width, hand height). Coach the absolutes, allow style.
Quality beats quantity: fewer, focused swings in practice are more valuable than hundreds of unfocused swings.

skills.name: Batting: stride and launch (toe-touch) position
skills.recommended_camera: Side view (open side) at hip height; rear view to check stride direction.

checkpoints.description: Short, soft, controlled stride toward the pitcher; stride foot lands on the inside ball of the foot, slightly closed.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: stride length roughly 0-1 foot lengths beyond the stance width; lead toe angle ~30-60 deg closed relative to the pitcher line at landing

checkpoints.description: At toe-touch the hands stay back (separation/'launch position'): the front foot lands while the hands remain near the rear shoulder.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: at front-foot contact frame, wrist position has not moved forward of the rear shoulder

checkpoints.description: Head stays level from stance through stride (no lunge, no drop).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: vertical head displacement < ~5 cm and forward head travel no more than a few cm beyond the stride-foot/rear-foot midpoint

faults.name: Lunging / drifting forward
faults.video_signs: Head and chest move toward the pitcher with the stride; front knee travels past the front foot; hands move forward with the body.
faults.correction_cue: 'Stride, don't go - land with your weight still centered and your hands back.'
faults.why_it_matters: Committing weight early leaves no power for off-speed pitches and drops the eye level.

faults.name: Late or no stride (timing)
faults.video_signs: Front foot is still in the air when the swing must start; rushed or arm-only swings.
faults.correction_cue: 'Get your foot down early - be on time, then let it go.'
faults.why_it_matters: Sequencing can only start once the front foot is down and braced.

faults.name: Stepping in the bucket (open stride)
faults.video_signs: Front foot lands well toward the pull-side foul line; front shoulder flies open.
faults.correction_cue: 'Stride toward the pitcher - land closed.'
faults.why_it_matters: Early opening pulls the barrel off the ball, especially on outside pitches.

drills.name: Two-plate timing drill (Coach Strub, NFCA)
drills.setup: Two home plates set in line: a back plate (simulates slower pitch) and a front plate (simulates faster pitch). Use BP or live pitching.
steps: Hitter starts at the front plate and takes rounds of swings.
Move to the back plate for the next round.
Progress to switching plates pitch-to-pitch.
Goal: be on time from either plate.
drills.dosage: 2-3 rounds of 5-6 swings per plate; finish with alternating pitches
drills.why: Changing the effective pitch speed forces the hitter to own the timing of the load/stride, the root cause of most lunges and late swings.

pro_tips.tip: A hitter is in charge of her own timing: drills that change the distance or speed of the pitch make the hitter adjust the stride, rather than the coach adjusting the hitter.
Earleywine lists 'toe touch or launch position' as its own phase - freeze-frame video at front-foot contact to check that the hands have not started forward.

skills.name: Batting: rotation, bat path and contact
skills.recommended_camera: Side view (open side) and front view from the pitcher's direction (behind a screen) at 120-240 fps.

checkpoints.description: Kinematic sequence: hips start rotating first, then core, then shoulders, then hands and barrel.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: pelvis rotation angle (line through hips, top view/front view) leads shoulder-line rotation; pelvis angular velocity peaks before shoulder angular velocity, which peaks before wrist speed

checkpoints.description: Rear heel rises and the rear foot pivots ('laces toward the pitcher') as the rear hip drives forward.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: rear heel lifts off the ground before contact; rear knee moves forward/down toward the front knee

checkpoints.description: Front leg firms up (braces) at or just before contact, stopping forward movement so the body rotates around it.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: lead knee angle increases (extends) between front-foot contact and ball contact, approaching ~160-180 deg

checkpoints.description: Hands stay inside the ball and above the barrel through the hitting zone, contacting the ball at a consistent contact spot out in front of the plate.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: at contact, wrists are at or above barrel height; contact point is in front of the lead hip for middle/inside pitches

checkpoints.description: Head stays still and eyes on the contact point.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: nose position at contact within a few cm of its position at front-foot contact

faults.name: Casting (long swing)
faults.video_signs: Hands move away from the body early; lead arm straightens early; the barrel makes a big arc ('sweeping') before reaching the zone.
faults.correction_cue: 'Knob to the ball - keep your hands inside.'
faults.why_it_matters: A long path is slower to contact and reduces bat control, especially on inside pitches.

faults.name: Arms-only swing / no hip rotation
faults.video_signs: Shoulders and arms start the swing while hips stay square; rear foot stays flat.
faults.correction_cue: 'Hips, core, shoulders, then hands.'
faults.why_it_matters: Without a proximal-to-distal sequence, bat speed and power drop sharply.

faults.name: Dropping the back shoulder / uppercut collapse
faults.video_signs: Rear shoulder dips sharply, rear knee collapses, barrel drops under the ball producing pop-ups.
faults.correction_cue: 'Stay through the ball - turn, don't dip.'
faults.why_it_matters: Excess shoulder tilt puts the barrel under the ball's plane.

faults.name: Inconsistent contact spot
faults.video_signs: Contact occurs at varying depths - sometimes deep beside the body, sometimes reaching out front.
faults.correction_cue: 'Find your spot and hit there every time.'
faults.why_it_matters: A repeatable contact point is what makes a swing reliable against varying pitches.

drills.name: Road Map (contact-spot) drill (NFCA)
drills.setup: Place a marker (ball or object) on the ground at the hitter's ideal contact spot; front toss.
steps: Hitter identifies her ideal contact spot and marks it.
Take front-toss reps, staying grounded and making contact at the marked spot.
Coach reports where contact actually occurred.
Adjust marker for inside/outside pitches once consistent.
drills.fixes: Inconsistent contact spot; casting; stepping in the bucket
drills.why: An external landmark gives the hitter a concrete target, so she learns the feel of contacting the ball at the same depth instead of chasing it.

drills.name: Two-tee bat-path drill
drills.setup: Two tees in line with the pitch path: the back tee (with ball) at the contact point and a second tee about 12-18 in. in front of it, set at the height of the desired path through the zone.
steps: Hit the ball off the back tee.
The barrel must travel on line through the space of the front tee (hit both balls or drive the first through the second's position).
Start slowly; increase speed when the path is consistent.
drills.fixes: Casting; bat wrap; dropping back shoulder
drills.why: The second tee defines a correct path through the zone, giving immediate feedback when the barrel sweeps around or dips under the ball.

drills.name: Slow-motion PVC sequencing drill
drills.setup: Hitter holds a light PVC pipe or bat in stance; no ball.
steps: Load and stride slowly.
Rotate hips first and pause.
Let the core and shoulders follow and pause.
Finally bring the hands/barrel through.
Gradually blend into one fluid motion, then hit off a tee.
drills.dosage: 2 sets x 10 slow reps then 10 tee swings
drills.why: Separating each link lets the athlete feel the hips-core-shoulders-hands order before speed hides the sequence.

pro_tips.tip: Coach Chidester (NFCA): after loading and getting the foot down, sequencing comes next - hips, core, shoulders, then hands and barrel.
Use a progression: tee for grip/stance/load/bat path, front toss for timing and contact spot, then live pitching for pitch recognition.
USA Softball national-team evaluators score hitting on mechanics, power and timing, and record exit velocity off a tee - measurable outcomes worth tracking alongside form.

skills.name: Batting: extension and follow-through
skills.recommended_camera: Side view and front view at normal speed; freeze 2-3 frames after contact.

checkpoints.description: Both arms extend through the ball after contact (extension), not before.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: both elbow angles reach near-full extension (~160-180 deg) shortly AFTER contact

checkpoints.description: Balanced finish: weight over a braced front leg, rear foot on its toe, belly button facing the pitcher, head still looking at the contact point.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: at finish, hip midpoint is between the feet (not behind the rear foot); pelvis faces the pitcher (~90 deg rotation from stance)

faults.name: Pulling off / early head pull
faults.video_signs: Head and front shoulder rotate away before contact; eyes leave the contact point.
faults.correction_cue: 'See the ball hit the bat; keep your chin in after contact.'
faults.why_it_matters: Pulling the head drags the front shoulder and barrel off the ball.

faults.name: Off-balance finish (falling back or forward)
faults.video_signs: Hitter falls toward the plate or backward after the swing; rear foot comes off the ground entirely or front foot spins open.
faults.correction_cue: 'Finish tall and hold it for a two-count.'
faults.why_it_matters: Balance at the finish reflects whether rotation happened around a stable axis.

drills.name: Tee swings with a 2-count finish hold
drills.setup: Tee at the hitter's contact spot.
steps: Swing at game speed.
Hold the finish for a two-count: weight over a firm front leg, rear foot on its toe, belly button to the pitcher, eyes at the contact point.
Coach or video checks the frozen finish.
drills.why: A held finish exposes balance and head-pull problems that are invisible at full speed.

pro_tips.tip: Earleywine lists extension and finish as separate phases of the swing: extension is where the barrel stays on the ball's line the longest.

skills.name: Windmill pitching
skills.recommended_camera: Side view from the open (glove) side at ~10-15 m, 120-240 fps; rear view from behind the pitcher to check the power line.

checkpoints.description: Drive off the rubber with the push-off leg; stride straight toward home along the 'power line'.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: stride-foot landing within ~1 foot-width of a line from the rubber to home plate (rear view)

checkpoints.description: Arm circle stays close to the body and in a vertical plane, passing through a tall 12 o'clock ('K' position) with the arm extended.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: throwing elbow angle ~160-180 deg at the 12 o'clock frame; wrist path stays within a near-vertical plane (front/rear view)

checkpoints.description: At stride-foot contact the trunk is not leaning back; moderate forward trunk flexion is associated with lower shoulder distraction force.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: trunk (hip-midpoint to shoulder-midpoint) at foot contact upright to slightly forward, not tilted back toward 2nd base

checkpoints.description: Firm landing on the stride leg: the front leg accepts large braking forces (vertical and braking ground reaction forces exceed body weight in youth pitchers).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: stride knee flexion stays controlled (no collapse > ~45 deg additional flexion after contact); knee tracks over the foot

checkpoints.description: Release near the hip with a quick wrist snap; arm finishes up/through rather than stopping abruptly.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: throwing wrist passes within ~1 hand-width of the throwing-side hip at release

faults.name: Stride off the power line
faults.video_signs: Stride foot lands well to the throwing-arm side or glove side of the rubber-to-plate line; body rotates open early.
faults.correction_cue: 'Drive down the line - land on the line.'
faults.why_it_matters: Off-line strides force the arm to compensate, hurting location and loading the shoulder.

faults.name: Leaning back at foot contact
faults.video_signs: Trunk tilts toward second base when the stride foot lands; pitch rides high.
faults.correction_cue: 'Land tall-to-forward; chest over the stride knee at release.'
faults.why_it_matters: Less trunk flexion at foot contact was associated with higher shoulder distraction force in high-school pitchers.

faults.name: Bent-arm / wide arm circle
faults.video_signs: Elbow bends at the top of the circle or the arm swings out away from the body.
faults.correction_cue: 'Big, tall circle, close to your body.'
faults.why_it_matters: A wide or bent circle is inconsistent and adds stress to the shoulder and biceps.

faults.name: Weak or no drive (arm-only pitch)
faults.video_signs: Little push-off; short stride; pitcher 'falls' forward and relies on the arm.
faults.correction_cue: 'Push the ground away - hips first.'
faults.why_it_matters: The lower body supplies the speed; an arm-only pitch is slower and puts more load on the arm.

drills.name: Wrist snaps -> half circles -> full circles
drills.setup: Pitcher stands with glove-side toward a partner/net at short distance (~6-8 m), stride already taken.
steps: Wrist snaps: from the hip, snap the ball to partner using only forearm/wrist.
Half circles: start the arm at 12 o'clock and pitch from there.
Full circles from the stride position.
Move back and add the stride only when each stage is consistent.
drills.fixes: Bent-arm / wide arm circle; inconsistent release
drills.why: Building the motion in layers grooves a repeatable release and circle before adding the stride and full-body speed.

drills.name: 'K' / power-position drill
drills.setup: Pitcher starts in the stride position with the arm at 12 o'clock (body forms a 'K').
steps: Hold the K position: arm extended overhead, glove pointing at the target.
Complete the downswing and release.
Check that the arm stays straight and close to the body.
drills.why: Isolating the top of the circle lets the pitcher feel an extended, vertical arm before the fast downswing.

drills.name: Power-line drive drill
drills.setup: Chalk or tape a line from the pitching rubber to home plate; optional low barrier or wall to drive toward.
steps: Drive off the rubber and stride with the stride foot landing on the line.
Freeze at foot contact and check trunk position (not leaning back).
Repeat with full pitch once footwork is consistent; film from behind.
drills.fixes: Stride off line; weak drive; leaning back
drills.why: A visible line gives immediate feedback on stride direction, and freezing at landing teaches the posture linked to lower shoulder load.

pro_tips.tip: Windmill pitching is NOT low-stress: shoulder distraction forces averaged ~80% of body weight in Olympic pitchers and ~94% in youth pitchers - similar to baseball pitchers. Manage pitch counts and rest.
The biceps works hardest (eccentrically) around the 9 o'clock phase and follow-through - include biceps/shoulder conditioning and watch for anterior shoulder pain.
National-team pitching evaluations grade speed, location and movement (5 pitches per pitch type with a called location) - film from behind the catcher to track location.

skills.name: Infield: fielding ground balls
skills.recommended_camera: Front view (from home plate direction) and side view at ground level.

checkpoints.description: Fielding position: feet staggered wider than shoulder width, glove-side foot slightly ahead; glove out in front at the 'top of the triangle' formed by the two feet.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: glove wrist forward of the line between the toes by roughly a forearm's length (triangle apex)

checkpoints.description: Low with hips and knees bent - glove starts on the ground and works up ('alligator' hands: glove below, throwing hand above).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: glove wrist starts near ground level; throwing hand above the glove at catch

checkpoints.description: Approach: use a drop step for balls to the forehand/backhand and work through the ball toward the target.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: first step opens toward the ball's path (hip rotation > ~30 deg on first step for balls hit to the side)

checkpoints.description: Transfer: both hands bring the ball to the throwing shoulder while the feet switch to an open throwing position with the front shoulder at the target.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: within ~0.5 s of the catch, ball hand at throwing-shoulder height and shoulder line pointing at target

faults.name: Fielding between the feet / too deep
faults.video_signs: Glove catches the ball underneath or behind the body, eyes not behind the ball.
faults.correction_cue: 'Glove out front - field at the top of the triangle.'
faults.why_it_matters: Fielding out front lets the eyes see the ball into the glove and leaves room for the hands to give.

faults.name: Bending at the waist with straight legs
faults.video_signs: Back rounded, knees nearly straight, glove reaching down from the waist.
faults.correction_cue: 'Get down with your legs, not your back.'
faults.why_it_matters: Straight legs make the fielder slow to adjust to bad hops and slow to transition to the throw.

faults.name: Slow transfer
faults.video_signs: Ball stays in the glove or the feet stay planted after the catch before the throw.
faults.correction_cue: 'Catch, pop the feet, ball to the shoulder.'
faults.why_it_matters: Every extra beat in the transfer is a step for the runner.

drills.name: Kneeling short-hop drill
drills.setup: Partners ~6 ft apart. Thrower kneels on throwing knee; fielder in fielding position.
steps: Thrower tosses short hops landing just in front of the fielder's 'triangle' apex.
Fielder fields out front with glove low, throwing hand above.
Progress: after the catch, 'pop' the feet to the open throwing position with the ball at the shoulder.
drills.why: Short distances give many fast, controlled reps to groove glove position and soft hands before full-speed grounders.

drills.name: 'Hot Dog' low-position drill (Megan Smith)
drills.setup: Partner rolls balls to the fielder.
steps: Fielder fields rolled balls in awkward positions (behind the back, between the legs) as described in the drill.
Emphasis: stay low and let the feet beat the hands.
drills.fixes: Bending at the waist; fielding too deep
drills.why: Forcing low, unusual catches builds leg-driven posture and footwork that 'beats the hands' to the ball.

drills.name: Rapid Fire (NFCA Drill 001)
drills.setup: Infielders in a line or pairs, coach/feeder with a bucket of balls.
steps: Feeder rolls/hits grounders in quick succession.
Fielder fields and throws back immediately.
Keep the drill time-boxed per the practice plan.
drills.dosage: Part of a 20-minute throwing & fielding block
drills.why: High-tempo reps reward a quick catch-to-throw transition under mild fatigue.

pro_tips.tip: Coach a short sequence: down, glove first, field, ball to the shoulder, throw.
Drop steps are used on both forehands and backhands; a good drop step is what increases an infielder's range.

skills.name: Overhand throwing (infield/outfield)
skills.recommended_camera: Side view from the glove side; front view from the target.

checkpoints.description: Front (glove) shoulder points to the target before the arm comes forward; weight starts on the inside of the back foot.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: shoulder line within ~20 deg of the throw direction at stride-foot contact

checkpoints.description: Infield throws use a three-quarter arm slot; a sidearm slot is reserved for rushed throws.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: forearm at release ~45 deg from vertical (3/4 slot)

checkpoints.description: Step toward the target and follow through, closing the distance to the target.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: stride foot lands on the line to the target (+/- ~15 deg); throwing hand finishes across to the glove-side hip

faults.name: Throwing open / all arm
faults.video_signs: Chest faces the target at release with no shoulder turn; little stride.
faults.correction_cue: 'Point your glove shoulder at the target, then turn.'
faults.why_it_matters: Without the turn and step, the arm supplies all the force - less velocity, more stress.

faults.name: Low/drop-down slot on routine throws
faults.video_signs: Elbow below shoulder height on routine throws; balls tail or sink.
faults.correction_cue: 'Three-quarter slot - elbow at or above the shoulder.'
faults.why_it_matters: A consistent 3/4 slot gives more accurate, carrying throws for infielders.

drills.name: Pop-feet to throwing position
drills.setup: Partner rolls balls side to side, ~6 ft away.
steps: Field the rolled ball at the top of the triangle.
'Pop' the feet into an open throwing position while bringing glove and ball to the throwing shoulder as fast as possible.
Front shoulder points at the partner; then complete the throw (or freeze for checks).
drills.fixes: Throwing open / all arm; slow transfer
drills.why: Linking the catch to a fast, aligned throwing position removes the dead time between fielding and throwing.

pro_tips.tip: Earleywine teaches infielders a 3/4 arm slot as the default and a sidearm throw only for rushed plays; good throwing mechanics also help keep players injury-free.
